# Analytics report-first selection

## Prospective scope and acceptance

The retained 390px partial-state [readiness screenshot](2026-09-22-analytics-report-readiness.md)
shows nearly an entire 1000px viewport of controls before the analytical explanation.
This owner-funded G3 refinement makes the selected report easier to reach, not a new
chart, workflow API, consumer migration or claim of faster human task completion.
Reference: Gallery reliability report informed by MatDash Dashboard2; preserve its
semantic light/dark tokens, system typography and direct data labels.

Starting revision: `b733566701187c726fd4ba6970b0768db3696cb7`.
Keep all native GET fields and current defaults. Put the existing filter form in
one initially closed native `details#analytics-selection`, with a 44px-minimum
keyboard-focusable summary, “Change comparison”, and the applied service group and
comparison. The selected month stays in the header. Do not hide the analytical
explanation or complete/missing/stale/partial warning inside this disclosure.
Keep the existing inner synthetic-condition and source disclosures, all URLs,
metric calculations, source/coverage rules, exports, themes and public APIs.
No application JavaScript, dependency or CSS generation change is planned.

Before any browser acquisition, freeze the changed sources, new test/driver,
this contract and reused ownership helper in a private input archive. Record
binary, compiled CSS, Node/Chrome/Playwright and input hashes. Preserve failed
executed inputs and reports independently of any correction.

Acceptance, fixed before acquisition:

- Static regression covers all 48 selections and relevant detail behavior: closed
  outer native disclosure, applied summary, labeled selected native controls,
  hidden theme, unchanged GET action and visible truth explanation outside it.
  Existing chart/table/CSV/source and refusal tests must still pass.
- Two fresh browser contexts: 1440×1000/light and 390×1000/dark, reduced motion,
  synthetic fixtures only. Observe complete/missing/stale/partial states; the
  390px August/API/no-comparison/partial explanation heading and truth label must
  fit within the first 1000px without opening a disclosure or scrolling.
- Native Tab/Enter opens “Change comparison”; native selection/Apply produces
  August/API/no-comparison/partial with exact Gateway/Search `At least 4`/`At least 2`.
  Gateway detail/back preserve this selection. CSV retains the expected context,
  counts and 33-column schema; no calculation or export-policy change.
- Require 44px summary target, visible keyboard focus, no outer horizontal overflow,
  correct theme and readable warning. Exact script-denying CSP, no application
  scripts or external requests. Keep 32KiB HTML and 160KiB HTML+CSS limits; no new
  latency/speedup, mobile-hardware, screen-reader or broad accessibility claim.
- Own a copied Gallery on its printed ephemeral loopback address and fresh Chrome;
  bound workload and cleanup using the existing owned-child helper. Require clean
  exits, output drainage and refused final listener. Existing previews remain alone.
- Stop after the two-lane acquisition, focused package checks and independent review.
  At most one harness-correction replay; retain any failed observation. A genuine
  product failure requires repair against the unchanged requirement, not a weaker gate.

## Result

`run-01` passes both native keyboard journeys, all eight initial state observations
and sixteen complete HTML/CSS navigation phases. Main visually reviewed the initial
partial-state screenshot in each lane. At 390px, the closed summary is 68px tall, the
explanation heading ends at 507px and the partial-state label ends at 702px. Both fit
the predeclared first 1000px constraint. No outer horizontal overflow was observed.
The complete warning and recovery link are visible in the inspected mobile capture;
this is not proof of faster comprehension or broader accessibility.

September/API complete rows retain 4/1 current, 6/3 previous and 2 fewer for each service.
Native selection changes to August/API/no-comparison/partial, showing `At least 4`
and `At least 2`; Gateway detail and Back preserve the full selection and theme.
Both native CSV downloads are identical, with the 33-column header, both expected
counts and selected period/source/coverage/role fields. This probe does not assert
every metadata cell's complete text. Existing package tests retain broader agreement,
missingness, escaping and refusal coverage.

Every navigation has exactly two completed HTTP 200 GET bodies, unchanged source CSS,
the exact script-denying CSP and no app scripts. Maximum HTML is 30,622B; HTML+CSS
is 81,995B, within 32KiB/160KiB. Native focus has a visible outline and a ≥44px summary.
Node 26.3.0, Chrome 153.0.8010.53 and Playwright 1.62.1 were recorded; all nine selected
input hashes match before/after. Chrome and Gallery exit 0 without forced termination
or truncated capture, and the owned listener refuses connection afterwards.
No existing preview, consumer, dependency, global configuration or live data changed.

Human A/B, broader G3/G4 acceptance and consumer/versioned propagation remain open.
Historical browser/performance receipts apply only to their original subjects; this
layout change does not inherit their runtime measurements. The maintained `quality.mjs`
adds native opening before filter selection; it was syntax-checked, not matrix-replayed.
Frozen historical readiness and usability-pair drivers remain unchanged.
